problem: Consider the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}28 & -7 & 14 \\ -4 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}]$ and the vector $b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ k \\ -1\end{aligned}].$ Find the value of $k$ such that $b\in \text{Null}(A).$

activity_context.topic_title: The Null Space of a Matrix

examples.knowledge_point: Solve a Variable in a Vector Lying in the Null Space of a Given Matrix
examples.problem: Consider the matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/a8b13d238a1e77d90abe70a505c68a72060ea95fe545f56ae53e7cf40ba0595e.png) and the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064430/assets/6e9f6c010c3137438923dfc32674dedf6d2d554b9b0a6745b007d826954d1e65.png) Find the value of $k$ such that $\mathbf{b}\in\textrm{Null}(A).$
examples.worked_solution:
If $\mathbf{b} \in \textrm{Null}(A),$ then we must have $A\mathbf{b} = \mathbf{0}.$ Substituting the given information, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Ab & =0 \\ [\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & -4 \\ -3 & 3 & -1 \\ 6 & -6 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ k \\ 3\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6+2k-12 \\ -6+3k-3 \\ 12-6k+6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

This corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2k-6=0 \\ 3k-9=0 \\ -6k+18=0\end{aligned}
$$

and for each of these equations, we obtain $k=3.$

feedback.problem:
The matrix $A$ and vectors ${b}_{1}$, ${b}_{2}$, ${b}_{3}$ are given below. Which of the vectors lie in $\text{Null}(A)?$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 6 & -10 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6\end{aligned}]
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
A vector $b$ lies in $\text{Null}(A)$ if $Ab=0.$ So, we need to compute the product of $A$ and each of the given vectors and check whether it is equal to $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A{b}_{1} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 6 & -10 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ 3\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 90\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 6 & -10 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8 \\ -7\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-59 \\ 118 \\ -33\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times  \\ A{b}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 6 & -10 \\ 9 & 15\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}10 \\ 6\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 180\end{aligned}]\ne 0\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, none of the vector lies in $\text{Null}(A).$
